newsitem.title: ITALY: JUDGE RULES FOR CECCHI GORI ON ITALY SOCCER RIGHTS.
newsitem.headline: JUDGE RULES FOR CECCHI GORI ON ITALY SOCCER RIGHTS.

text.p: A judge ruled on Wednesday that the rights to broadcast Italian league soccer on regular television should go to media tycoon Vittorio Cecchi Gori rather than state broadcaster RAI.

The decision, which remains provisional pending a final verdict and evidence that Cecchi Gori has the funds to buy the rights, marked the latest round in a battle between the owner of Italy's two private TeleMonteCarlo channels and RAI.
A spokeswoman for Cecchi Gori Communications said company officials were deliberating the implications of the judge's ruling and there was no immediate comment.

Cecchi Gori, who also owns first division soccer club Fiorentina, was awarded the tv and radio rights at the end of February after he offered the soccer league 213.5 billion lire ($135 million) a year for exclusive coverage.
RAI offered only 185 billion lire ($118 million) in the secret auction and the prospect of losing the rights, which it has always held, sent shock waves through the company.
RAI, which is funded both by a licence fee and advertising, had argued that it has a duty to show soccer because of its position as a public service broadcaster.

However, Cecchi Gori's stations, whose signals cannot be received throughout all of Italy, failed to deposit bank guarantees to cover the bid and offered in March to withdraw their offer "as a sign of responsibility".
In April, RAI said it had regained the rights after further discussions with the Milan-based soccer league.
But Cecchi Gori challenged the move and police impounded documents relating to the controversial auction.
The judge ruled that Cecchi Gori had until March 20, 1997, to present the financial sureties requested by the league at the time of the original bidding.
The rights do not cover pay-per-view screening of Italian league soccer, broadcast in coded form, which belong to the Telepiu 2 channel.
